title: api: standardize Retry-After + idempotency semantics for streaming and OpenAI compatibility
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: Inconsistent rate-limit and idempotency behavior between the Redwood API and our OpenAI-compat endpoints caused client-side retries to double-submit work and led to streaming sessions being terminated without clear guidance. This PR unifies Retry-After header semantics, formalizes error codes for rate limits and service availability, and extends idempotency handling to streaming and function-calling flows so clients can safely retry or resume streams. Summary of changes: 1) HTTP: ensure 429 and 503 responses include a standardized Retry-After header (seconds or HTTP-date) and a machine-readable JSON field `retry_after_seconds` for clients that cannot parse HTTP-date; 2) Error codes: introduce consistent error code namespace values `rate_limit_exceeded`, `service_unavailable`, and `idempotency_conflict` across both Redwood-native and OpenAI-compat endpoints; 3) Idempotency: expand our idempotency key validation to streaming creation requests (both websocket and chunked HTTP streaming). If a previously completed request is retried with the same idempotency key, servers now return the final result (or a stream-resumption token when the previous run partially completed) rather than starting a duplicate run; 4) Streaming resumption: add a resumable token header (`X-Redwood-Resume-Token`) that is issued on partial stream failures and returned to clients so they can resume without re-executing the model; 5) SDK and docs: update TS/Python SDKs and API docs to expose retry-after helpers and resume APIs; 6) OpenAI-compat layer: map OpenAI error shape to the unified codes/headers while preserving compatibility for existing clients. Backwards compatibility and rollout: default behavior is backward-compatible for clients that ignore new headers; we added feature flags and a gradual rollout to Dedicated clusters. Testing: unit tests for header emission, integration wiring tests for OpenAI-compat mapping, end-to-end streaming resumption test harness, and flaky-test suppression added for known infra timing. Rollout plan: staged release behind a runtime feature flag, Canary + Dedicated pilot, SDK patch releases, and final flag removal after 4 weeks of stable telemetry. Related work: ENG-2345 (rate-limits spec), ENG-2410 (streaming resumable design), SUP-448 (customer incident), INT-92 (internal tooling for retry metrics).
commits: standardize: emit Retry-After header on 429/503 responses
streaming: add resume token generation and validation
idempotency: extend validation to streaming create endpoints
openai-compat: translate error shapes and include retry_after_seconds
sdk: expose retry helpers in ts/python sdks
docs: add retry semantics and streaming resume guide
tests: add unit/integration/e2e tests for retry/idempotency/resume
ci: adjust flaky suppression for new streaming tests
review_comments: Lina Chen: Can you clarify the exact Retry-After semantics for sub-second waits? Maya Patel: We emit seconds as integers for sub-minute waits and HTTP-date for long waits; clients should prefer retry_after_seconds if present.

Ravi Singh: Concern about cost metrics if resumed streams are double-billed. Maya Patel: Resume token includes original request id and server-side attribution; billing pipeline will dedupe based on the request id and resume token mapping.
Jordan Blake: Please add a migration note for Dedicated customers. Maya Patel: Added a rollout/migration section and a feature-flag for Dedicated clusters in the PR description.

Lina Chen (requested changes): Add a unit test for idempotency_conflict when a second simultaneous request with same key arrives. Maya Patel: Added a test in idempotency suite and fixed a race by serializing key creation.
Ravi Singh (approval): Tested on canary cluster; Retry-After header present and SDK helpers worked as expected. LGTM.
ci_checks: bench: skipped (not required for this change)
release_notes: Standardized Retry-After and idempotency semantics across streaming, function calling, and OpenAI-compat endpoints. Added Retry-After header and retry_after_seconds payload, unified error codes (rate_limit_exceeded, service_unavailable, idempotency_conflict), and streaming resume tokens to allow safe resumption of partially completed streams. SDKs updated with helpers.
notes: This change is rolled out behind a runtime feature flag and applied to Hosted and Canary clusters first. Dedicated customers will be migrated with opt-in before enforced. SDK patch releases accompany this PR. Monitoring/alerts added for retry spikes and duplicate billing risk.
